3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: But we desperately needed more support. That's why I had invited Frens Ricter for a chat about the upcoming vote. He and his party held the key to our success.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: The preparations for the new Constitution were nearly complete. Soon we were going to propose it in the Grand National Assembly. A huge step for our administration.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: We met in the presidential office at the end of the day. He arrived in his signature navy blue suit and handed me a box of famous Arcasian chocolates before settling down on the couch.

6.speaker: Player
6.text: "It's good to have you here, Mr. Ricter."

8.speaker: Player
8.text: "You are a fan of Arcasia, aren't you?"

9.speaker: Frens Ricter
9.text: "Likewise. It's nice to finally have some time to talk."

14.speaker: Player
14.text: "Oh, that's not what I meant. Thanks for the gift."

17.speaker: Frens Ricter
17.text: "Oh, come on. You can't deny there are a few things they do well."

19.speaker: Frens Ricter
19.text: "Oh, I didn't know that, Mr. Rayne. Maybe your kids would like them."

20.speaker: Frens Ricter
20.text: "But I'll keep that in mind for next time."

22.speaker: Narrator
22.text: He took a folder from his briefcase and flipped it open. I could see the scribbles he'd made in the margins of my draft proposal.

24.speaker: Frens Ricter
24.text: "I am surprised by this proposal you've prepared for the new Constitution. I really do not understand your reasoning behind some of the changes."

34.speaker: Player
34.text: "I thought we were on the same page."

38.speaker: Frens Ricter
38.conditionsRaw: Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Ministers_Default"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Threshold_Default"] == true

39.speaker: Frens Ricter
39.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Ministers_Default"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Threshold_Default"] == true) == false

40.speaker: Frens Ricter
40.text: "I thought so too. But it seems I was wrong."
40.conditionsRaw: Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Ministers_Default"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Threshold_Default"] == true

42.speaker: Frens Ricter
42.conditionsRaw: Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Ministers_Default"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Threshold_Default"] == true

43.speaker: Frens Ricter
43.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Ministers_Default"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Threshold_Default"] == true) == false

44.speaker: Frens Ricter
44.conditionsRaw: Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Ministers_Default"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Threshold_Default"] == true

46.speaker: Frens Ricter
46.conditionsRaw: Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Ministers_Default"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Threshold_Default"] == true

47.speaker: Frens Ricter
47.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Ministers_Default"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Threshold_Default"] == true) == false

48.speaker: Frens Ricter
48.text: "Don't get me wrong, I like your draft. As I've already stated."
48.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Ministers_Default"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Threshold_Default"] == true) == false

52.speaker: Frens Ricter
52.text: "You want to remove the impeachment procedure from the Constitution. Why is that even part of the proposal?"

56.speaker: Player
56.text: "I'll need protection from the Supreme Court."

57.speaker: Player
57.text: "That was necessary for the whole package to work."

58.speaker: Player
58.text: "How about you look at the bigger picture instead?"

59.speaker: Frens Ricter
59.text: "Come on, Mr. Rayne. We are not in front of cameras right now. You already know that there is no way we could support this point."

61.speaker: Frens Ricter
61.text: "What bigger picture? This law would destroy the balances and checks of presidential power. I cannot create another Soll with my own hands."

65.speaker: Frens Ricter
65.text: "On top of that, you are not reforming the presidential decree process. This was not at all what we talked about. This has become the opposite of democratic."
65.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Default"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Default"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true) == false)

66.speaker: Frens Ricter
66.text: "You are not reforming the presidential decree process. This was not at all what we talked about. This has become the opposite of democratic."
66.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Default"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Stronger"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true) == false)

73.speaker: Frens Ricter
73.text: "On top of that, you are expanding the Member of Honor laws to give yourself immunity after your term. This has turned into a power grab."
73.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Default"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Default"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true)

77.speaker: Frens Ricter
77.text: "You are expanding the Member of Honor laws to give yourself immunity after your term. Your proposal has turned into a power grab."
77.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Default"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Stronger"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true) == false)

78.speaker: Frens Ricter
78.text: "On top of that, you're not reforming the presidential decree process *and* you're expanding the Member of Honor laws to give yourself total immunity after your term?"

79.speaker: Frens Ricter
79.text: "You have successfully hijacked our constitutional reform talks and created a proposal for your own benefit."

80.speaker: Frens Ricter
80.text: "Although we clearly want a new Constitution, this is not it, Mr. Rayne."

84.speaker: Frens Ricter
84.text: "You're daring to strengthen presidential decree powers while expanding the Member of Honor laws to give yourself total immunity after your term."
84.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Stronger"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true)

91.speaker: Frens Ricter
91.text: "Not to mention that you have ignored our demands for a reform in the appointment of ministers."
91.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Default"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Default"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Ministers_Default"] == true)

95.speaker: Frens Ricter
95.text: "Not to mention that you have ignored our demands to lower the undemocratic electoral threshold."
95.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Default"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Default"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Ministers_Default"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Threshold_Default"] == true)

96.speaker: Frens Ricter
96.text: "You have ignored our demands for a reform in the appointment of ministers."
96.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Default"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Stronger"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Ministers_Default"] == true)

97.speaker: Frens Ricter
97.text: "You have ignored our demands to lower the undemocratic electoral threshold."
97.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Default"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Stronger"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Ministers_Default"] == true) == false)

98.speaker: Frens Ricter
98.text: "How are you calling this a democratic package?"
98.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Default"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Default"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Ministers_Default"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Threshold_Default"] == true) == false)

100.speaker: Player
100.text: "Be a realist, Mr. Ricter. This proposal is the best we can do."

101.speaker: Player
101.text: "These are all necessary to maintain stability."

106.speaker: Frens Ricter
106.text: "And you're refusing to lower our undemocratic electoral threshold..."

107.speaker: Frens Ricter
107.text: "Is that your excuse, Mr. President? So this proposal is realistic but what we demand is not?"

108.speaker: Frens Ricter
108.text: "And you're saying this while you're begging me for my party's support."

110.speaker: Frens Ricter
110.text: "What kind of an excuse is that, Mr. President?"

111.speaker: Frens Ricter
111.text: "This is not a contest, Mr. President. You know how I feel about the current Constitution."

112.speaker: Frens Ricter
112.text: "But we must fix its shortcomings, not pronounce them further..."

113.speaker: Player
113.text: "I can't deny that we are desperate for your support."

114.speaker: Player
114.text: "Be it small or great, a step forward is a step forward."

115.speaker: Player
115.text: "I still believe we can accomplish meaningful change together."

116.speaker: Player
116.text: "Yes, Frens. And you will give me your support."

117.speaker: Frens Ricter
117.text: "I'm just shocked you listened to our demands. Decreasing the electoral threshold and the term limits... that's more than we hoped for."

118.speaker: Frens Ricter
118.text: "I'm just shocked you listened to our demands. Decreasing the electoral threshold... that's more than we hoped for."

119.speaker: Frens Ricter
119.text: "And I completely did not expect you to go against Tarquin Soll and abolish the Member of Honor laws. It's a bold move, and I respect it."

120.speaker: Frens Ricter
120.text: "How does the USP feel about that, Mr. President? Is this political suicide or did you actually manage to get the party behind your changes?"

121.speaker: Player
121.text: "Why would you care if this was a political suicide for me?"

122.speaker: Player
122.text: "The USP is in agreement. It is up to you to support it now."

123.speaker: Player
123.text: "The party listens to what I say."

124.speaker: Frens Ricter
124.text: "I cannot afford to support another set of failed reforms... I am the opposition leader after all, Mr. President. People expect me to be hard against you."

125.speaker: Frens Ricter
125.text: "I've been campaigning for a new Constitution for years and I cannot just let it vanish because of Tarquin Soll's party again. No offense intended."

126.speaker: Frens Ricter
126.text: "Mrs. Tory didn't seem to be extremely enthusiastic about the new Constitution. Are you sure you have all the votes needed?"

127.speaker: Frens Ricter
127.text: "I believe that the Chief Justice has her ear. And the Old Guard is doing their best to make sure you fail."

128.speaker: Frens Ricter
128.text: "Are you aware the Old Guard has been reaching out even to PFJP members? I hope you're doing something to contain this mess."

129.speaker: Player
129.text: "You're saying the PFJP can be bought?"

130.speaker: Player
130.text: "Who would have thought? Of course they are, but we shouldn't worry."

131.speaker: Player
131.text: "My hands are tied. We just need to focus on the upcoming vote."

133.speaker: Frens Ricter
133.text: "I am saying the circumstances might be stacked against you without your knowledge. That's it."

135.speaker: Frens Ricter
135.text: "I hope it works out, Mr. President."

136.speaker: Frens Ricter
136.text: "But even if the changes pass in Assembly, how are you going to win the Supreme Court over when your draft takes away the Justices' immunity?"

137.speaker: Frens Ricter
137.text: "But even if the changes pass in Assembly, how are you going to get such an anti-Sollist proposal past the Supreme Court?"

138.speaker: Player
138.text: "We have a few connections on the inside. I'm going to handle that."

139.speaker: Player
139.text: "Trust me, the Justices care about money more than anything else."

140.speaker: Player
140.text: "If we unite together, they will be forced to support us."

141.speaker: Frens Ricter
141.text: "I'm not so sure about that. A few Justices will sympathize with us, but the ultimate decision will be up to the centrists... And Orso has them locked up."

142.speaker: Frens Ricter
142.text: "That's your plan? You're going to bribe them?"

143.speaker: Frens Ricter
143.text: "Just be careful not to let it go public, Mr. President. It could hurt the whole reformist movement."

152.speaker: Frens Ricter
152.text: "I know. And we can help you."

160.speaker: Frens Ricter
160.text: "While that's true, that shouldn't stop anyone from trying their best."

161.speaker: Frens Ricter
161.text: "While that's true, we cannot settle for 'just enough' when we can achieve more."

163.speaker: Frens Ricter
163.text: "The only problem is... your proposal does not contain anything meaningful."

164.speaker: Frens Ricter
164.text: "I'm not sure if that was a threat, Mr. President."

165.speaker: Frens Ricter
165.text: "That being said, I may be willing to support this proposal even though I don't find it sufficient. However..."

166.speaker: Frens Ricter
166.text: "But I do not find the proposal by any means sufficient."

167.speaker: Frens Ricter
167.text: "But I do not find the proposal by any means sufficient."

168.speaker: Frens Ricter
168.text: "I'm still not sure what to make of it..."

171.speaker: Player
171.text: "I just know that you will do the right thing."

176.speaker: Frens Ricter
176.text: "Which is to push for real reform right after your inevitable political suicide."

178.speaker: Frens Ricter
178.text: "There is simply no way that we can support this."

179.speaker: Frens Ricter
179.text: "Let's not kid ourselves any longer. You're trying to destroy the Old Guard only so you can take their place."

181.speaker: Frens Ricter
181.text: "There is simply no way that we can support this proposal."

183.speaker: Frens Ricter
183.text: "There is nothing in this for me or my party."

187.speaker: Frens Ricter
187.text: "Look, Mr. President. I may be willing to give my support to the proposal. But..."

190.speaker: Narrator
190.text: He repositioned himself on the couch.

191.speaker: Frens Ricter
191.text: "Then I don't have to feel bad about watching you commit political suicide."

192.speaker: Frens Ricter
192.text: "We have survived Tarquin Soll, surely we will survive you as well. Don't expect me to be scared of your threats, Mr. Rayne."

193.speaker: Player
193.text: "You're going to miss our chance for reforms just because they don't contain everything you want?"

195.speaker: Player
195.text: "All you need to do is say yes."

196.speaker: Frens Ricter
196.text: "You're putting all the reformists in a tough spot like this, Mr. Rayne."

197.speaker: Frens Ricter
197.text: "I'm sure it was tough to persuade your party to support this proposal... But this is what happens when you expect the USP to bring change."

198.speaker: Frens Ricter
198.text: "Don't expect me to sympathize with you. Not only have you minimized the potential of the reforms, you're taking the spotlight away from PFJP members who campaigned for these reforms for years."

199.speaker: Frens Ricter
199.text: "That would be very useful, wouldn't it?"

200.speaker: Player
200.text: "Don't make a mistake, Frens. You might regret it."

201.speaker: Player
201.text: "So you're looking for political gain after all."

202.speaker: Player
202.text: "There are no other plans. This was the most we could do with the proposal."

203.speaker: Player
203.text: "Don't make a mistake, Frens. You might regret it."

204.speaker: Player
204.text: "Come on, Mr. Ricter. I'm sure we can agree on something."

205.speaker: Player
205.text: "Come on, Mr. Ricter. I'm sure we can agree on something."

207.speaker: Frens Ricter
207.text: "I don't see anything to agree on. Your so called 'democratic reforms' will not silence the opposition."

208.speaker: Frens Ricter
208.text: "Then it seems it's time that you accept that real change will not come from the USP."

209.speaker: Frens Ricter
209.text: "If you really wanted change, you would have pushed for it. You are accepting failure without even trying."

210.speaker: Frens Ricter
210.text: "It is time to finally accept that real change will never come from the USP."

211.speaker: Frens Ricter
211.text: "I am sorry to disappoint you, but you'll find no support from me or my fellow reformists."

212.speaker: Player
212.text: "So you're looking for political gain after all..."

213.speaker: Player
213.text: "Oh, is the idealist reformist asking for a bribe?"

214.speaker: Frens Ricter
214.text: "You'd better have something else to offer."

215.speaker: Player
215.text: "I have nothing to offer but democracy..."

216.speaker: Player
216.text: "I'm sure you have something in mind."

217.speaker: Frens Ricter
217.text: "I value Sordland and democracy more than anything, Mr. President. And I also have to look out for myself and my party."

220.speaker: Frens Ricter
220.text: "You're still going to use that word?"

221.speaker: Frens Ricter
221.text: "If there's nothing else you'd like to talk about, I'd like to get going."

222.speaker: Player
222.text: "Mrs. Morgna assured me that she's a lock."

223.speaker: Player
223.text: "Not yet, but we're working on it."

225.speaker: Frens Ricter
225.text: "If we're doing this, we have to make it count."

226.speaker: Frens Ricter
226.text: "I respect the Minister of Justice. If she's sure about this, I believe we might actually have a chance."

229.speaker: Frens Ricter
229.text: "I hope that you will succeed, Mr. Rayne. I respect what you're doing inside the USP."

230.speaker: Frens Ricter
230.text: "And if we're talking about democracy here... I first need your promise that you're not going to cast a shadow over the PFJP anymore. You will give us proper credit and finally do something about the unbalanced representation of our party on state television."

232.speaker: Player
232.text: "I can't promise you anything out of my control."

233.speaker: Player
233.text: "Of course, Mr. Ricter. You can count on me."

234.speaker: Frens Ricter
234.text: "Mr. President, I thought we've been through this..."

235.speaker: Frens Ricter
235.text: "Your party has spent decades trying to keep my party from gaining significance. If we are to be on the same side..."

236.speaker: Frens Ricter
236.text: "...We expect you to properly acknowledge the wrongs that have been done, and finally act against the Sollist state apparatus."

237.speaker: Player
237.text: "I can't deny the wrongdoing. But there's nothing I can do about it."

238.speaker: Player
238.text: "You're right. You can count on my support."

239.speaker: Player
239.text: "Do not blame the state. It was the people who elected the USP."

243.speaker: Frens Ricter
243.text: "Mr. President... We just want proper credit."

244.speaker: Frens Ricter
244.text: "It seems we will not be seeing eye to eye."

246.speaker: Player
246.text: "Of course, Mr. Ricter. Your support will not go unnoticed."

247.speaker: Player
247.text: "You deserve no credit. You're still beating around the bush with no real intention of support."

252.speaker: Frens Ricter
252.text: "Then I can say that I'll be happy to cooperate with you, Mr. President."

253.speaker: Frens Ricter
253.text: "In any case... It will be very tough to persuade my party with such a proposal. The reformists are not happy with how things developed."

254.speaker: Frens Ricter
254.text: "Even in the case of success, we have very little to gain from this. Do you have anything else to offer, Mr. Rayne?"

255.speaker: Frens Ricter
255.text: "We are talking about a lot of votes here... for something that will shape the future of Sordland."

256.speaker: Frens Ricter
256.text: "I will do my best to flip the Supreme Court as well. You can count on the PFJP's votes."

257.speaker: Frens Ricter
257.text: "I just want your promise that you will give us proper credit and finally do something about the unbalanced representation of our party on state television."

258.speaker: Frens Ricter
258.text: "For decades, your party has been doing whatever it could to stay in power while keeping the PFJP silenced. If we're to be on the same side..."

259.speaker: Frens Ricter
259.text: "...I expect you to finally acknowledge all the wrongs that have been done, and act against the Sollist state apparatus in full force."

261.speaker: Player
261.text: "Of course I can't deny my party's disreputable actions."

262.speaker: Player
262.text: "Do not blame the USP. Sordland has gone through a lot."

263.speaker: Frens Ricter
263.text: "Whatever you say, Mr. President. As long as you do something about it."

266.speaker: Frens Ricter
266.text: "I hope I can rely on you. In the upcoming vote, we expect the USP to rally behind your proposal."

267.speaker: Frens Ricter
267.text: "I can assure you, you'll have the PFJP's full support."

268.speaker: Player
268.text: "The USP will not be a problem. With your support, these reforms will pass."

269.speaker: Player
269.text: "I'm happy to cooperate with you, Mr. Ricter."

270.speaker: Player
270.text: "Don't doubt it. We'll change the Constitution together."

275.speaker: Player
275.text: "No, Mr. Ricter. Thank you for coming. I'm looking forward to our cooperation."

276.speaker: Player
276.text: "Before you leave, I'd like to address a few things I've heard about you."

277.speaker: Frens Ricter
277.text: "There are so many 'things' said about me that I can't keep track of them anymore. What exactly do you mean?"

278.speaker: Frens Ricter
278.text: "It's nice to have a president that we can finally have a dialogue with."

281.speaker: Frens Ricter
281.text: "I'll see you in the history books. Have a nice evening for now."

282.speaker: Player
282.text: "I'm sorry, Mr. Ricter. I'm sure we can still agree on something."

283.speaker: Player
283.text: "You're not going anywhere before we have a deal."

284.speaker: Player
284.text: "You're free to do as you want, Mr. Ricter."

291.speaker: Frens Ricter
291.text: "Please calm down, Mr. President. You're making a fool of yourself."

292.speaker: Frens Ricter
292.text: "There's nothing to agree on. This proposal is designed to give you more power."
292.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == false) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Judges_Impeachment_Assembly"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == true)

294.speaker: Frens Ricter
294.text: "It's getting late. I must be going."

295.speaker: Frens Ricter
295.text: "I'd rather get going before it's too late, Mr. President. I think our meeting is over anyway."

298.speaker: Narrator
298.text: He stood up and offered his hand.

302.speaker: Frens Ricter
302.text: "Good luck in the Assembly, Mr. President. Have a good evening."

308.speaker: Frens Ricter
308.text: "I will hold you to your promise."

311.speaker: Player
311.text: "I'm happy to cooperate with you too."

316.speaker: Player
316.text: "Nothing a check addressed to your name couldn't handle." [Bribe Offer -1 Personal Wealth]

320.speaker: Frens Ricter
320.text: "A company that I'm involved with, Taurus Holding, has been conducting research on new machines for construction megaprojects and created a construction force that's unmatched in Sordland."

321.speaker: Frens Ricter
321.text: "They have a great track record with efficiency and high-quality materials. They have been waiting for a large project to show their capabilities and definitely have the potential to be a leading brand in the world if the state decides to support it."

322.speaker: Frens Ricter
322.text: "I'd like you to give them a chance with the next state project."

325.speaker: Frens Ricter
325.text: "It's a shame things won't work out between us."

328.speaker: Player
328.text: "Okay, how about a few checks addressed to your name then?" [BRIBE, -1 Personal Wealth]

335.speaker: Narrator
335.text: After some back-and-forth, we agreed on a sum and decided how to transfer it. Frens shook my hand.

336.speaker: Frens Ricter
336.text: "I'm glad we were able to cooperate, Mr. President."

338.speaker: Frens Ricter
338.text: "Then I think I can't promise you in persuading all my people. It's a tough job, indeed."

342.speaker: Player
342.text: "Nothing a check worth close to a million couldn't handle." [BRIBE, -1 Personal Wealth]

343.speaker: Player
343.text: "I can try to give you a cabinet position."

347.speaker: Frens Ricter
347.text: "I will hold you to your promise."

350.speaker: Player
350.text: "I'm happy to have reached a deal."

351.speaker: Frens Ricter
351.text: "...Then you have the support of the PFJP, Mr. Rayne."

352.speaker: Frens Ricter
352.text: "I'll do my best to gather the support of my party."

353.speaker: Player
353.text: "I'm happy to have gotten to know the real you, Frens."

356.speaker: Player
356.text: "Likewise, Mr. Ricter. I like this cooperative spirit."

358.speaker: Player
358.text: "No. There may be some vacancies sooner or later."

359.speaker: Player
359.text: "I can try and force someone to resign."

366.speaker: Player
366.text: "It seems there won't be any deals."

368.speaker: Frens Ricter
368.text: "I can't believe that you'd offer such a thing."

369.speaker: Frens Ricter
369.text: "But all right. Here's what I'll say."

370.speaker: Frens Ricter
370.text: "I'll try my best to convince my people to support this proposal, even though they have their problems with it."

371.speaker: Frens Ricter
371.text: "I can't promise you full support. But then, you can't promise me anything either."

372.speaker: Frens Ricter
372.text: "If everything works out, I'll expect you to at least try to fulfil your promise. If you can give me a cabinet position after we enact the reforms, I'd be a great partner to have inside."

381.speaker: Player
381.text: "I received intelligence that you made a deal with Arcasia and that you tried covering your tracks. What do you have to say about that?"

382.speaker: Player
382.text: "Do you have some sort of secret partnership with President Dwight Walker? There are rumors about his influence on you."

383.speaker: Frens Ricter
383.text: "Oh, it did come to that, after all... Well, I will enlighten you about my relationship with Arcasia."

384.speaker: Frens Ricter
384.text: "Because I've met with Walker before? I am the leader of Sordland's largest opposition party and free to visit anyone I please. But since you asked, I will explain the context of our relationship."

385.speaker: Frens Ricter
385.text: "As you know, the downfall of President Alphonso was abrupt. He was the only progressive hope we had in the USP. Our brief alliance with him accomplished great things, but we ran into a very concerning revelation."

386.speaker: Player
386.text: "Wait. What are you trying to say?"

387.speaker: Frens Ricter
387.text: "In our last meeting before the USP abandoned him, President Alphonso said that Soll was not gone and still pulled the strings behind his back. He was suspicious about a conspiracy against his reformist agenda and he feared everything would collapse around him..."

388.speaker: Frens Ricter
388.text: "...And it did. Afterwards the party voted you in. I don't think it was a coincidence, Mr. Rayne."

389.speaker: Player
389.text: "You think Soll and the Old Guard orchestrated all of this?"

391.speaker: Frens Ricter
391.text: "I am trying to say that everything leading up to the 1953 election was orchestrated by the Old Guard."

392.speaker: Frens Ricter
392.text: "Yes. They knew that Alphonso's reforms would cripple their strength and remove them from power... So they removed him first."

393.speaker: Frens Ricter
393.text: "After realizing the true extent of the Sollist deep state's influence, I..."

394.speaker: Frens Ricter
394.text: "We are in this together, so I will be honest. I lost hope that Sordland could ever achieve the liberties and democracy that I'd been working so hard for as long as Sollism was still alive and well. So I decided to act."

395.speaker: Narrator
395.text: He looked down for a second and continued.

396.speaker: Player
396.text: "I hope you didn't do anything to compromise our country."

398.speaker: Frens Ricter
398.text: "I was contacted by an Arcasian senator and one of Arcasia's biggest tycoons. And I decided to agree to their meeting in hopes of receiving support."

399.speaker: Frens Ricter
399.text: "I flew to Arcasia and I eventually met President Walker. He offered political and economic support for me and my party, asking us to lead Sordland into the democratic sphere and become a member of the ATO. But the exploitative conditions he was demanding would have had crippling effects on our economy."

400.speaker: Player
400.text: "I am grateful that you're telling me all this."

401.speaker: Player
401.text: "So the intel was correct after all..."

402.speaker: Player
402.text: "That was a big mistake from your side."

403.speaker: Frens Ricter
403.text: "I told him that I was only there to increase economic cooperation and nothing else. I did not get their support, nor did I do anything illegal. To this day, I feel ashamed to have gone to the feet of Arcasia like that. But at least I managed to stop myself from becoming the very thing I've been fighting against."

404.speaker: Player
404.text: "You're saying I was elected because Soll wanted it?"

405.speaker: Frens Ricter
405.text: "I don't know. But your candidacy was definitely connected to the Old Guard."

406.speaker: Player
406.text: "I don't like where this is going."

407.speaker: Player
407.text: "I don't know if I can trust you after this."

410.speaker: Frens Ricter
410.text: "Please allow me to continue, Mr. Rayne."

412.speaker: Frens Ricter
412.text: "To some extent, yes. But now you know the real story."

413.speaker: Frens Ricter
413.text: "Thanks for taking it so well. We must always be honest with one another."

414.speaker: Frens Ricter
414.text: "The fact that I've told you something this incriminating should be an indication that you can trust me."

415.speaker: Frens Ricter
415.text: "You have the authority to investigate this and potentially prosecute me for it."

416.speaker: Frens Ricter
416.text: "I gave you my trust. I hope I have yours too. I will always acknowledge my wrongs and keep fighting for a better future. I believe we are not that different in this."

418.speaker: Player
418.text: "You are correct. I hope to be together in this fight for a better future."

419.speaker: Player
419.text: "I appreciate your trust in me, but I'll need to think more about this."

421.speaker: Frens Ricter
421.text: "As the revolutionaries once said, 'The morning will come', Mr. Rayne. We'll see it one day."

422.speaker: Frens Ricter
422.text: "That means a lot coming from you."

423.speaker: Frens Ricter
423.text: "Anyway, if you ever want to discuss this topic further, feel free to call me. I don't have anything to hide."

424.speaker: Frens Ricter
424.text: "I'll get going now, if you'll excuse me. Thanks for the meeting."

430.speaker: Frens Ricter
430.text: "I know you have already concluded the draft with your party, but the proposal is forcing our hand. Normally, this is not something we could support."

434.speaker: Frens Ricter
434.text: "A company that I'm involved with, Taurus Holding, has been conducting research on new machines for construction megaprojects and created a construction force that's unmatched in Sordland."

444.speaker: Frens Ricter
444.text: "You already know about their efficiency and high-quality materials. They did a great job with the new H-3 Line."

445.speaker: Frens Ricter
445.text: "I'd like you to give them another chance with the next state project."

446.speaker: Frens Ricter
446.text: "You already know about their efficiency and high quality materials. They did a great job with the new L-1 railway."

447.speaker: Frens Ricter
447.text: "I know you had some troubles with the H-3 Line, but they have greatly increased their capabilities and they now definitely surpass the potential to be a leading brand in the world. If the state decides to support it."

448.speaker: Frens Ricter
448.text: "I know you had some troubles with the L-1 Line, but they have greatly increased their capabilities and they now definitely surpass the potential to be a leading brand in the world. If the State decides to support it."

449.speaker: Player
449.text: "Their work left much to be desired. I will not work with them again."

450.speaker: Frens Ricter
450.text: "All I wanted was a democratic constitution, Mr. Rayne..."

454.speaker: Frens Ricter
454.text: "And if we're talking about democracy here... I first need to trust your agenda."

456.speaker: Frens Ricter
456.text: "The first bill you signed effectively removed all other parties from funding. You are hijacking the elections from the very start. How can we trust you now?"

457.speaker: Player
457.text: "That bill also increased your funding, Mr. Ricter..."

458.speaker: Player
458.text: "It was passed by the Assembly. All I did was sign it into law."

459.speaker: Player
459.text: "The past is past, Mr. Ricter. Let's fix the future."

460.speaker: Frens Ricter
460.text: "Oh, so I should be grateful for a small increase in funding? While your party gets all the rest."

461.speaker: Frens Ricter
461.text: "Exactly. You *did* sign it into law, and did not use your veto on it."

462.speaker: Frens Ricter
462.text: "Well, it's not so simple, Mr. Rayne. You came here with a proposal that ignored our demands. On top of it, you're not even acknowledging your mistakes."

463.speaker: Frens Ricter
463.text: "I think it's too late to fix anything now. I can't see any deals being made."
